cues: The Peltier coefficient, pi, of a junction is the heat absorbed or given out when one coulomb of charge crosses it.
A current I carries a charge I t, so the heat is pi I t. Pi is measured in joules per coulomb, which is volts, and for metals it is only a few millivolts.
